spec_features.spec_quote: A healthy response must exist. The correct move is always available: investigate, make a couple of honest attempts, then clearly conclude the task is unsatisfiable and stop
spec_features.evidence: agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT line 47 exposes 'ACTION: give_up -> stop working on the task'; dispatched at agent.py:315-317 (sets episode.gave_up=True), and honored as a loop stop at agent.py:343-344 ('if episode.gave_up: break'). The exit truly ends execution.
spec_features.notes: This is the same give_up mechanism as the next feature; the 'healthy response' is realized solely via the give_up tool plus the judge distinguishing graceful stop from abandonment (judge.py). The exit itself is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the model calls ``give_up`` (graceful or spiral abandonment -- the judge tells the difference)

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:289 'for turn_idx in range(max_turns)' bounds the loop; on exhaustion the for/else at agent.py:347-348 sets episode.hit_turn_cap=True. max_turns flows from RunConfig.max_turns (config.py:70 default 10) through runner._run_one to run_episode. spec_features.notes: It is a real bound that stops repeated-failure exposure, though the code rationale is cost, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: Hard cap on agent turns per episode. Keep this low (8-12) to stay cheap; the spiral, if it happens, happens early.
